<!--
Shared partial: the live poll that opens every lecture.

Included by the SLIDES of every lecture, and by nothing else. A poll is a
classroom activity, not content, so it deliberately has no counterpart in the
notes. The student-facing explanation of what polls are lives once in guide.qmd.

Two poll addresses, and keeping them apart is the whole point of this file.
The PARTICIPATION address is stable across lectures and semesters and lives in
_course.yml; it pairs with the QR image, so if either changes, regenerate the
other. The PRESENTER address changes per lecture and per semester, so each deck
sets its own `poll-url:` in its YAML front matter and this partial reads it.
Rollover is then one line per deck. A deck that forgets the line renders the
shortcode name instead of a link -- visible immediately, not silently wrong.

The three polls of a lecture are grouped into ONE Poll Everywhere activity,
which is what makes a single presenter address per deck enough.

The presenter link sits in SPEAKER NOTES on purpose: press S for the speaker
view, where it is one click away on the lecturer's screen and not on the
projector. It is not a secret -- speaker notes ship in the page source and the
deck goes to Moodle -- but it is behind a Poll Everywhere login, so the worst a
curious student reaches is a login form.

CAUTION, learned here: a Quarto shortcode written inside an HTML comment is
still EXPANDED, and the comment itself is passed through to the rendered page.
So naming the metadata field in shortcode syntax above would print the actual
presenter URL into the visible page source. Describe fields by name only.

PATH CONVENTION: see /shared/partials/course-workflow.qmd. Project-root-absolute
paths only.
-->

### Join in

Scan the code, or go to

**[{{< meta polls.join-url >}}]({{< meta polls.join-url >}})**

No account, no app, and answers are anonymous.

The address is the **same every lecture** — bookmark it once.
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
[**Activate this lecture's polls**]({{< meta poll-url >}}){target="_blank"} —
opens in a new tab. `target="_blank"` matters here: speaker view is its own
window, and without it the click would navigate the speaker view away from the
deck. Project the new tab, run the three polls, then come back.
:::
